title: Local manifest
description: manifest.json in the local data directory: every place the command-line program wrote to on this computer. Uninstalling and drift detection look at nothing else. A manifest that cannot be read or does not match this schema is unknown, never empty.

schema.description: The version of the manifest format. This schema describes version 1.

rgd.description: The version of the command-line program that last wrote the manifest.

source.description: Where the resources came from at the last sync.

type.description: "server" for a team server, "repo" for a resource repository read directly.

url.description: The address of the server or repository.

entries.description: One entry per place written, in the order they were written.

toolId.description: The identifier of a tool adapter, such as "claude-code".

path.description: A path with forward slashes on every platform. A path inside the home directory starts with "~/" and is expanded on use, so the manifest survives a renamed user or a moved home directory.

base64.description: Bytes in the standard base64 encoding (RFC 4648, with padding), which is how encoding/json writes a byte slice.

argv.description: A command and its arguments, run as they are, without a shell.

id.description: Identifies the target: tool, operation and place, such as "claude-code:tree:~/.claude/skills/<name>". Unique in the manifest.

resource.description: The code of the resource this entry delivers.

version.description: The published version of the resource. 0 or absent when the resource came straight from a repository.

op.description: What was written: "tree" a directory of ours, "file" a file of ours, "key" one key in a tool's configuration file, "exec" something installed with the tool's own command.

path.description: The directory or file written, or for "key" the configuration file.

format.description: The syntax of the configuration file. Only for "key".

key.description: The key that was set, one element per level; a key name may itself contain dots. Only for "key".

digest.description: The digest of what was written, for detecting later changes. "tree": the content digest of the directory; "file": the SHA-256 of the file; "key": the SHA-256 of the key's value as canonical JSON.

backup.description: Where the configuration file was copied before it was first changed, relative to the local data directory. Only for "key". A backup is for a person to restore by hand; undoing an entry never copies it back.

undo.description: The command that reverses the installation. Only for "exec".

sharedWith.description: Other tools that read this entry's directory and therefore did not get a copy of their own.

created.description: Directories that did not exist and were created to hold the target, outermost first. Undoing the entry removes them again, innermost first, as long as they are empty. For "key" it also lists the configuration file itself when the file did not exist; undoing removes the file when nothing but the key was in it.

edit.description: How to take a key that was added out of its file again, byte for byte: in the file as written, "new" starts at "offset" and replaced "old". While "new" is still there, undoing puts "old" back; otherwise the key is removed by its meaning. Only for "key", and only when the key was added rather than changed. Absent in manifests written before it existed: the key is then removed by its meaning.

offset.description: Where "new" starts in the file, in bytes, counting a byte order mark.

old.description: The bytes that were replaced, base64-encoded; empty when the edit only inserted text.

new.description: The bytes that were written, base64-encoded.

created.description: How many trailing elements of "key" did not exist before: 1 for the key alone, 2 when its parent was created too, and so on. Undoing removes those parents again if they are empty.

at.description: When the entry was written, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
